title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Company Formation
text:
Company Formation

Key terms: Board of Directors, Limited Liability, Perpetual Succession

A company is formed by law, with capital contributed by shareholders who elect a Board of Directors to manage it. It's a separate legal entity with limited liability, perpetual succession, and a common seal.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Company Formation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital
text:
Share Capital

Key terms: Authorized Capital, Issued Capital, Paid Up Capital

Share capital is the money contributed by shareholders in exchange for shares. It's divided into categories like authorized, issued, subscribed, called up, paid up, and uncalled capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Kinds of Companies
text:
Kinds of Companies

Key terms: Limited Liability, Public Company, Private Company

Companies can be classified based on the liability of their members (limited by shares, guarantee, or unlimited) or the number of members (public, private, or one-person company).

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Kinds of Companies in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Preference Shares
text:
Preference Shares

Key terms: Preferential Right, Cumulative, Redeemable

Preference shares have a preferential right to dividend and capital repayment. They can be participating, cumulative, or redeemable.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Preference Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Equity Shares
text:
Equity Shares

Key terms: Equity Shareholder, Differential Rights

Equity shares don't have preferential rights. Their dividend varies and they may have differential rights as per the company's Articles of Association.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Equity Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital Issue Process
text:
Share Capital Issue Process

Key terms: Prospectus, Minimum Subscription, Allotment

The process of issuing shares to the public involves several steps: issuing a prospectus, receiving applications, and making allotments. The company must receive a minimum subscription within a specified time frame.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Capital Issue Process in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital Instalments
text:
Share Capital Instalments

Key terms: Par Value, Premium, Instalments

Shares can be issued at par or at a premium, and the capital can be collected in instalments. The first instalment is collected with the application, and the remaining instalments are collected later.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Capital Instalments in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Accounting for Share Application
text:
Accounting for Share Application

Key terms: Share Application Account, Share Capital Account

When shares are applied for, the application money is initially credited to a share application account. This account is later closed by transferring the balance to the share capital account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Accounting for Share Application in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Allotment of Shares
text:
Allotment of Shares

Key terms: Allotment Money, Share Allotment Account

When shares are allotted, the allotment money is received, and the share application account is closed. Any excess application money is adjusted towards the amount due on allotment.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Allotment of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Calls
text:
Share Calls

Key terms: Share Call, Uniform Basis, Notice

Share calls are instalments of the share capital that are due after the initial application and allotment. Calls must be made on a uniform basis and with adequate notice to shareholders.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Calls in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Accounting for Share Calls
text:
Accounting for Share Calls

Key terms: Share Call Account, Journal Entry

When a share call is made, a journal entry is passed to record the call money due. When the call money is received, another journal entry is passed to record the receipt.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Accounting for Share Calls in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Applications Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA)
text:
Applications Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA)

Key terms: ASBA, Blocked Amount, Allotment

ASBA is a process where applicants authorise their bank to block the application money in their account until the allotment of securities. If securities are not allotted, the block is removed.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Applications Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA) in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Application and Allotment
text:
Share Application and Allotment

Key terms: Share Application, Allotment, Share Capital

When shares are offered for subscription, applicants pay an initial amount (application money). If their application is successful, they pay the allotment money. The company records these transactions in the Share Application and Allotment accounts.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Application and Allotment in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Calls
text:
Share Calls

Key terms: Share Calls, First Call, Second and Final Call

Share calls are installments of the share price that shareholders pay after the initial application and allotment. The company records these transactions in separate call accounts (First Call, Second and Final Call, etc.).

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Calls in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Calls in Arrears
text:
Calls in Arrears

Key terms: Calls in Arrears, Unpaid Calls, Interest on Calls in Arrears

When shareholders fail to pay their share calls on the due date, the unpaid amount is recorded as 'Calls in Arrears'. The company may charge interest on these amounts until they are paid.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Calls in Arrears in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Calls in Advance
text:
Calls in Advance

Key terms: Calls in Advance, Interest on Calls in Advance

When shareholders pay their share calls before they are due, the amount is recorded as 'Calls in Advance'. The company may pay interest on these amounts until they are used to pay the due calls.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Calls in Advance in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Journal Entries for Share Capital Transactions
text:
Journal Entries for Share Capital Transactions

Key terms: Journal Entries, Debit, Credit, Share Capital Accounts

The company records share capital transactions using journal entries. These entries involve debits and credits to various share capital accounts, such as Share Application, Share Allotment, Share Calls, and Calls in Arrears/Advance.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Journal Entries for Share Capital Transactions
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Journal Entries for Share Capital Transactions in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Allotment
text:
Share Allotment

Key terms: allotment, applicant, share, distribution

The process of distributing shares to applicants after the application period has closed. The company decides how many shares each applicant receives based on the number of shares applied for and the total number of shares available.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Allotment in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital
text:
Share Capital

Key terms: share capital, equity, balance sheet

The total amount of money invested in a company by its shareholders in exchange for shares. It represents the company's equity and is shown on the balance sheet as share capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Share Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Application
text:
Share Application

Key terms: application, application fee, refundable

The process of applying for shares in a company. Applicants pay an application fee, which is usually refundable if their application is not successful.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Application in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Call
text:
Share Call

Key terms: call, installment, final call

A demand for additional payment by shareholders to fully pay for their shares. Calls are typically made in installments, with the final call being the last payment required to fully pay for the shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Call in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Over Subscription
text:
Over Subscription

Key terms: over subscription, excess applications, pro-rata allotment

A situation where the number of shares applied for exceeds the number of shares offered for subscription. The company must decide how to deal with the excess applications, such as accepting some applications in full and rejecting others, making a pro-rata allotment, or using a combination of these methods.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Over Subscription in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Under Subscription
text:
Under Subscription

Key terms: under subscription, minimum subscriptions, refund

A situation where the number of shares applied for is less than the number of shares offered for subscription. The company must refund the entire subscription amount received and may need to seek additional subscriptions to meet the minimum required amount.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Under Subscription in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Shares at a Premium
text:
Issue of Shares at a Premium

Key terms: premium, nominal value, securities premium account

When shares are issued at a price higher than their nominal or par value. The premium amount is credited to a separate account called 'Securities Premium Account' and can only be used for specific purposes, such as issuing fully paid bonus shares or writing off preliminary expenses.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Issue of Shares at a Premium
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Issue of Shares at a Premium in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Shares Issued at a Premium
text:
Shares Issued at a Premium

Key terms: Share Premium, Securities Premium Reserve

When shares are issued for more than their face value, the extra amount is called a premium. This premium is credited to the Securities Premium Reserve account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Shares Issued at a Premium in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Shares Issued for Consideration Other Than Cash
text:
Shares Issued for Consideration Other Than Cash

Key terms: Issue Price, Consideration

Sometimes, shares are issued in exchange for assets or services instead of cash. The number of shares issued is calculated based on the issue price and the amount payable.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Shares Issued for Consideration Other Than Cash
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Shares Issued for Consideration Other Than Cash in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares
text:
Forfeiture of Shares

Key terms: Forfeiture, Share Capital, Calls Account

If shareholders fail to pay their calls, their shares can be forfeited. The amount paid is transferred back to the relevant calls account, and the share capital is reduced by the called-up amount.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Private Placement of Shares
text:
Private Placement of Shares

Key terms: Private Placement, Offer Letter

Private placement involves offering securities to a select group of investors through a private placement offer letter. It's an alternative to public offerings.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Private Placement of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Employees Stock Option Plan (ESOP)
text:
Employees Stock Option Plan (ESOP)

Key terms: ESOP, Grant Date, Vesting Period

ESOP allows companies to offer shares to employees at a lower price than the market value. It's a form of compensation and has specific grant, vesting, and exercise conditions.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Employees Stock Option Plan (ESOP) in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Premium
text:
Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Premium

Key terms: share forfeiture, share capital, securities premium reserve

When shares are issued at a premium and some are forfeited, the premium amount received is not debited from the Securities Premium Reserve Account. The forfeiture entry is made only on the Share Capital Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Premium
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Premium in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Discount
text:
Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Discount

Key terms: share forfeiture, share discount, share capital

When shares are issued at a discount and some are forfeited, the discount amount received is not credited to the Share Capital Account. The forfeiture entry is made only on the Share Discount Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Discount
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares Issued at a Discount in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Pro-rata Allotment
text:
Pro-rata Allotment

Key terms: pro-rata, allotment, application money

When the number of applications exceeds the number of shares available, shares are allotted in proportion to the number of shares applied for. Excess application money is adjusted towards allotment.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Pro-rata Allotment in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Reissue of Forfeited Shares
text:
Reissue of Forfeited Shares

Key terms: reissue, forfeited shares, capital reserve

Forfeited shares can be reissued at par, premium, or discount. The maximum discount allowed on reissue cannot exceed the amount received on the forfeited shares. Any remaining balance in the Share Forfeiture Account is transferred to the Capital Reserve Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Reissue of Forfeited Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Journal Entry for Forfeiture of Shares
text:
Journal Entry for Forfeiture of Shares

Key terms: journal entry, share capital, share forfeiture

The journal entry for forfeiture of shares involves debiting the Share Capital Account and crediting the Share Forfeiture Account. If the shares were issued at a premium or discount, the Securities Premium Reserve Account or Share Discount Account may also be affected.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Journal Entry for Forfeiture of Shares
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Journal Entry for Forfeiture of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Calls
text:
Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Calls

Key terms: share forfeiture, non-payment of calls, share capital

When shares are forfeited due to non-payment of calls, the Share Capital Account and the Share Forfeiture Account are debited. If the shares were issued at a premium and the premium has not been fully received, the Securities Premium Reserve Account is also debited.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Calls
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Calls in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Allotment Money
text:
Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Allotment Money

Key terms: share forfeiture, non-payment of allotment money, share allotment

When shares are forfeited due to non-payment of allotment money, the Share Allotment Account and the Share Forfeiture Account are debited. If the shares were issued at a premium or discount, the Securities Premium Reserve Account or Share Discount Account may also be affected.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Allotment Money
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares due to Non-payment of Allotment Money in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Reissue after Forfeiture
text:
Share Reissue after Forfeiture

Key terms: Share Forfeiture, Reissue, Capital Reserve

When shares are forfeited due to non-payment of calls, they can be reissued at a later date. The profit on reissue is transferred to the capital reserve.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Reissue after Forfeiture in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Proportionate Transfer to Capital Reserve
text:
Proportionate Transfer to Capital Reserve

Key terms: Proportionate, Capital Reserve, Share Forfeiture Account

When only a part of the forfeited shares are reissued, only the proportionate amount of the share forfeiture account balance should be transferred to the capital reserve.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Proportionate Transfer to Capital Reserve in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Journal Entry for Share Forfeiture
text:
Journal Entry for Share Forfeiture

Key terms: Journal Entry, Share Forfeiture, Share Capital

When shares are forfeited, a journal entry is made to record the loss of capital and the amount forfeited is transferred to the share forfeiture account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Journal Entry for Share Forfeiture in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Journal Entry for Share Reissue
text:
Journal Entry for Share Reissue

Key terms: Journal Entry, Share Reissue, Capital Reserve

When forfeited shares are reissued, a journal entry is made to record the reissue and the profit on reissue is transferred to the capital reserve.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Journal Entry for Share Reissue in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital Transactions
text:
Share Capital Transactions

Key terms: Share Capital, Issuance, Allotment, Forfeiture, Reissue

Share capital transactions include issuance of shares, receipt of application money, allotment of shares, receipt of call money, forfeiture of shares, and reissue of forfeited shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Share Capital Transactions in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital
text:
Share Capital

Key terms: Share, Shareholder, Capital

The total amount of money a company raises by issuing shares to its shareholders. It's the foundation of a company's financial structure.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Issue Procedure
text:
Share Issue Procedure

Key terms: Issue, Application, Allotment, Call

The process of a company collecting share capital by issuing shares to the public or a select group of individuals. It involves stages like application, allotment, and calls on shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Issue Procedure in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Calls in Arrears
text:
Calls in Arrears

Key terms: Call, Arrears, Unpaid

The unpaid amount due on shares, which can accumulate over time if not paid by the shareholders. It's not mandatory for a company to maintain a separate account for this.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Calls in Arrears in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Calls in Advance
text:
Calls in Advance

Key terms: Call, Advance, Interest

An amount paid by a shareholder in excess of the amount due on their shares. A separate account is maintained for this, and the company may pay interest on it.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Calls in Advance in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Over Subscription
text:
Over Subscription

Key terms: Subscription, Over, Under

A situation where the number of shares applied for exceeds the number of shares offered for subscription. It's the opposite of under subscription.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Over Subscription in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Shares at Premium
text:
Issue of Shares at Premium

Key terms: Premium, Issue, Securities Premium Reserve

Shares issued for an amount more than their nominal value. The premium amount is credited to the Securities Premium Reserve Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Issue of Shares at Premium in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Shares at Par
text:
Issue of Shares at Par

Key terms: par value, nominal value

Shares issued for an amount exactly equal to their face or nominal value. No premium or discount involved.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Issue of Shares at Par in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Shares at Premium
text:
Issue of Shares at Premium

Key terms: premium, Securities Premium Reserve Account

Shares issued for an amount more than their nominal value. The premium is credited to a separate account called 'Securities Premium Reserve Account'.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Issue of Shares at Premium in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Shares at Discount
text:
Issue of Shares at Discount

Key terms: discount, sweat equity shares

Shares issued for an amount less than their nominal value. The discount is debited to 'Discount on Issue of Share Account'. Only sweat equity shares can be issued at a discount.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Issue of Shares at Discount in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Forfeiture of Shares
text:
Forfeiture of Shares

Key terms: forfeiture, breach of contract

Cancellation of share allotment due to breach of contract, such as failure to pay installments. The amount already received on such shares is credited to 'Forfeiture Shares Account'.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Forfeiture of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Reissue of Shares
text:
Reissue of Shares

Key terms: reissue, Share Forfeiture Account

Reissuing shares once forfeited by the company. The discount allowed on reissue is debited to 'Share Forfeiture Account'.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Reissue of Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Public Company
text:
Public Company

Key terms: public invitation, minimum members, directors

A company that can invite the public to subscribe for its shares. It must have a minimum of seven members and three directors.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Public Company in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Private Company
text:
Private Company

Key terms: private invitation, minimum members, directors

A company that cannot invite the public to subscribe for its shares. It must have a minimum of two members and two directors.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Private Company in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Minimum Subscription
text:
Minimum Subscription

Key terms: minimum amount, nominal value, incorporation

The minimum amount of money that must be received from subscribers before a company can be incorporated. It must be at least 25% of the nominal value of the shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Minimum Subscription in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Allotment and Refusal
text:
Share Allotment and Refusal

Key terms: share allotment, oversubscription, pro-rata

When shares are oversubscribed, companies decide how to allot them. They may refuse allotment to some applicants, allot in full to others, and allocate the rest pro-rata.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Allotment and Refusal in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Forfeiture and Reissue
text:
Share Forfeiture and Reissue

Key terms: share forfeiture, capital reserve, share reissue

If shareholders fail to pay their due amounts, their shares can be forfeited and reissued. The difference between the forfeiture and reissue prices goes to capital reserve.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Share Forfeiture and Reissue in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Premium and Capital Reserve
text:
Share Premium and Capital Reserve

Key terms: share premium, capital reserve, nominal value

When shares are issued at a premium, the excess amount over the nominal value goes to share premium account. When forfeited shares are reissued at a lower price, the difference is transferred to capital reserve.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Share Premium and Capital Reserve in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Application Money Adjustment
text:
Share Application Money Adjustment

Key terms: share application, excess money, allotment

When applications for shares exceed the number available, excess application money can be adjusted against the sums due on allotment.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Application Money Adjustment in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Forfeiture and Reissue Journal Entries
text:
Share Forfeiture and Reissue Journal Entries

Key terms: journal entries, capital reserve, share forfeiture account

Journal entries are recorded to reflect the forfeiture and reissue of shares, including the transfer to capital reserve and the balance in share forfeiture account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Share Forfeiture and Reissue Journal Entries
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Share Forfeiture and Reissue Journal Entries in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital and Share Premium Account
text:
Share Capital and Share Premium Account

Key terms: share capital, share premium account, balance sheet

When shares are issued, the nominal value goes to share capital, and any premium to share premium account. These accounts are reflected in the balance sheet.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Share Capital and Share Premium Account
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Capital and Share Premium Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Forfeiture and Reissue Cash Book
text:
Share Forfeiture and Reissue Cash Book

Key terms: cash book, receipts, payments

The cash book records the receipts and payments related to share forfeiture and reissue, including the amounts received from reissuing forfeited shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Share Forfeiture and Reissue Cash Book
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Share Forfeiture and Reissue Cash Book in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Allotment and Refusal Test
text:
Share Allotment and Refusal Test

Key terms: true or false, test understanding

True or false statements about share allotment and refusal can be used to test understanding of the topic.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Share Allotment and Refusal Test in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Debenture Definition
text:
Debenture Definition

Key terms: debenture, interest, redemption

A debenture is a written contract acknowledging a debt, with a fixed interest rate, payable at specified intervals, and redeemable after a specified period.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Debenture Definition in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Debentures vs Shares
text:
Debentures vs Shares

Key terms: borrowed capital, ownership, interest, dividends, redemption

Debentures represent borrowed capital, while shares represent ownership. Debentures carry interest, while shares carry dividends. Debentures are redeemable, while shares are not.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Debentures vs Shares in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Secured vs Unsecured Debentures
text:
Secured vs Unsecured Debentures

Key terms: secured, unsecured, charge, floating charge

Secured debentures have a charge on the company's assets, while unsecured debentures do not. Unsecured debentures may have a floating charge.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Secured vs Unsecured Debentures in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Redeemable vs Irredeemable Debentures
text:
Redeemable vs Irredeemable Debentures

Key terms: redeemable, irredeemable, winding-up, specific period, long period

Redeemable debentures are payable on expiry of a specific period, while irredeemable debentures are repayable on winding-up or after a long period.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Redeemable vs Irredeemable Debentures in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Convertible vs Non-Convertible Debentures
text:
Convertible vs Non-Convertible Debentures

Periodic payment made by the company to the debentureholders as a fixed percentage of the face value of the debentures. It is a charge against the company's profit.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Issue of Debentures
text:
Issue of Debentures

When a company raises capital by selling debentures to the public, this is known as the issue of debentures. The company receives application money, which is then transferred to the debentures account and securities premium reserve account. text:

Interest on debentures is payable annually to the debenture holders. The journal entry involves debiting the debenture interest account and crediting the debenture holders account. The interest is then paid from the bank account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Debentures in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Redemption of Debentures
text:
Redemption of Debentures

Key terms: Redemption of Debentures, Premium on Redemption, Debentures Account

Redemption of debentures involves the company buying back its own debentures from the market or from the debenture holders. The journal entry involves debiting the debentures account and crediting the debenture holders account. Any premium on redemption is recorded in the profit and loss account.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Debenture Redemption Reserve
text:
Debenture Redemption Reserve

Key terms: Debenture Redemption Reserve, Outstanding Debentures

A debenture redemption reserve is a reserve created by a company to meet the future liability of redeeming its debentures. The reserve is created by transferring an amount equal to 10% of the outstanding debentures to the reserve account.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Debenture Redemption Reserve in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Debenture Redemption Investment
text:
Debenture Redemption Investment

Key terms: Debenture Redemption Investment, Debentures to be Redeemed

A debenture redemption investment is an investment made by a company to meet the future liability of redeeming its debentures. The investment is made at a rate of 15% of the debentures to be redeemed.

When a company buys back its own debentures for immediate cancellation, it records a profit or loss on redemption. If purchased at a price below nominal value, it's a profit; if above, it's a loss.

Financial statements are based on recorded facts, accounting conventions, postulates, and personal judgments. They reflect a combination of these elements and provide a periodical review of a company's financial position and results.

Key terms: Net Profit, Total Assets

Measures the profitability of a company's investments. Calculated as Net Profit / Total Assets.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Return on Investment (ROI) in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Purpose of Cash Flow Statement
text:
Purpose of Cash Flow Statement

Key terms: cash flow statement, cash inflows, cash outflows

A cash flow statement shows inflows and outflows of cash and cash equivalents from various activities of a company during a specific period. Its primary objective is to provide useful information about cash flows under operating, investing, and financing activities.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Purpose of Cash Flow Statement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash and Cash Equivalents
text:
Cash and Cash Equivalents

Key terms: cash, cash equivalents, liquid investments

Cash includes cash in hand and demand deposits with banks, while cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments that can be readily converted into known amounts of cash with an insignificant risk of changes in value.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cash and Cash Equivalents in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Classification of Cash Flows
text:
Classification of Cash Flows

Key terms: operating activities, investing activities, financing activities

Cash flows are classified into operating, investing, and financing activities to show separately the cash flows generated or used by these activities. This helps users assess the impact on the financial position and cash and cash equivalents.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Classification of Cash Flows in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flows from Operating Activities
text:
Cash Flows from Operating Activities

Key terms: operating activities, cash inflows, cash outflows

Operating activities are the primary or main activities of an enterprise, such as procurement of raw materials, manufacturing expenses, and sale of goods or services. Cash flows from operating activities are primarily derived from the main activities of the enterprise.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cash Flows from Operating Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flows from Investing Activities
text:
Cash Flows from Investing Activities

Key terms: investing activities, long-term assets, investments

Investing activities relate to the acquisition and disposal of long-term assets and other investments not included in cash equivalents. Separate disclosure of cash flows from investing activities is important as they represent the extent to which expenditures have been made for resources intended to generate future income and cash flows.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cash Flows from Investing Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flows from Financing Activities
text:
Cash Flows from Financing Activities

Key terms: financing activities, owners' capital, borrowings

Financing activities relate to changes in the size and composition of the owners' capital and borrowings of the enterprise. Separate disclosure of cash flows arising from financing activities is important as it helps predict claims on future cash flows by providers of funds.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cash Flows from Financing Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Preparation of Cash Flow Statement
text:
Preparation of Cash Flow Statement

Key terms: cash flow statement, direct method, indirect method

A cash flow statement can be prepared using either the direct method, which lists cash inflows and outflows, or the indirect method, which adjusts net income for non-cash items and changes in assets and liabilities.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Preparation of Cash Flow Statement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Tax Classification in Cash Flow Statement
text:
Tax Classification in Cash Flow Statement

Key terms: operating activities, financing activities, investing activities, capital gains tax, dividend tax

Taxes on income and gains should be classified as operating, financing, or investing activities based on their source. Tax on operating profit is operating cash flow, dividend tax is financing activity, and capital gains tax on fixed assets is investing activity.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Tax Classification in Cash Flow Statement
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Tax Classification in Cash Flow Statement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Non-Cash Transactions in Cash Flow Statement
text:
Non-Cash Transactions in Cash Flow Statement

Key terms: non-cash transactions, investing activities, financing activities, cash flow statement

Non-cash investing and financing transactions should be excluded from the cash flow statement and disclosed elsewhere in the financial statements. Assets acquired by issuing shares are not included in the cash flow statement due to their non-cash nature.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Non-Cash Transactions in Cash Flow Statement
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Non-Cash Transactions in Cash Flow Statement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow Statement Classifications
text:
Cash Flow Statement Classifications

Key terms: cash flow statement, operating activities, investing activities, financing activities, net increase/decrease in cash

A cash flow statement is divided into three main sections: cash flows from operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities. The net increase or decrease in cash and cash equivalents is the sum of these three sections.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Flow Statement Classifications in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Direct vs Indirect Method for Operating Cash Flows
text:
Direct vs Indirect Method for Operating Cash Flows

Key terms: direct method, indirect method, net profit, non-cash items, working capital

The direct method shows major classes of gross cash receipts and payments, while the indirect method adjusts net profit for non-cash items, changes in working capital, and items associated with investing or financing cash flows.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Direct vs Indirect Method for Operating Cash Flows
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Direct vs Indirect Method for Operating Cash Flows in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Adjusting Net Profit for Cash Flows
text:
Adjusting Net Profit for Cash Flows

Key terms: net profit, non-cash items, non-operating items, working capital, income tax paid

To calculate cash flows from operating activities using the indirect method, net profit is adjusted for non-cash items, non-operating items, changes in working capital, and income tax paid.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Adjusting Net Profit for Cash Flows
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Adjusting Net Profit for Cash Flows in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Proposed Dividend Accounting
text:
Proposed Dividend Accounting

Key terms: proposed dividend, contingent liability, dividend payable, financing activities

A proposed dividend is shown as a contingent liability in the notes to accounts and is accounted for as a dividend payable after it is declared by shareholders. It is shown as a cash outflow under financing activities in the cash flow statement.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Proposed Dividend Accounting in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Provision for Taxation
text:
Provision for Taxation

Key terms: Income Tax, Provision

A provision set aside to cover the expected income tax liability for the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Provision for Taxation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow from Operating Activities
text:
Cash Flow from Operating Activities

Key terms: Cash Inflow, Cash Outflow, Operating Activities

The cash generated or used in the normal business operations of a company.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Flow from Operating Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Depreciation
text:
Depreciation

Key terms: Asset, Useful Life, Depreciation Expense

The allocation of the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Depreciation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Goodwill Amortisation
text:
Goodwill Amortisation

Key terms: Goodwill, Amortisation, Useful Life

The systematic allocation of the premium paid for an acquisition over the expected useful life of the assets acquired.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Goodwill Amortisation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Gain on Sale of Machinery
text:
Gain on Sale of Machinery

Key terms: Selling Price, Carrying Amount, Gain

The profit made from selling machinery, calculated as the selling price minus the carrying amount.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Gain on Sale of Machinery in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow from Operating Activities
text:
Cash Flow from Operating Activities

Key terms: net income, non-cash items, working capital

Cash generated from core business operations, calculated as net income plus adjustments for non-cash items and changes in working capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Flow from Operating Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow from Investing Activities
text:
Cash Flow from Investing Activities

Key terms: long-term assets, property, plant, and equipment, investments

Cash used or generated from long-term assets, including purchases and sales of property, plant, and equipment, and investments.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Flow from Investing Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow from Financing Activities
text:
Cash Flow from Financing Activities

Key terms: financing sources, issuance and repayment of debt, payment of dividends, issuance of equity

Cash used or generated from financing sources, including issuance and repayment of debt, payment of dividends, and issuance of equity.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Flow from Financing Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Net Increase/Decrease in Cash and Cash Equivalents
text:
Net Increase/Decrease in Cash and Cash Equivalents

Key terms: cash and cash equivalents, opening balance, cash inflows, cash outflows

The change in cash and cash equivalents during the period, calculated as the opening balance plus cash inflows minus cash outflows.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Net Increase/Decrease in Cash and Cash Equivalents
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Net Increase/Decrease in Cash and Cash Equivalents in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash and Cash Equivalents at the End of the Period
text:
Cash and Cash Equivalents at the End of the Period

Key terms: closing balance, opening balance, net increase/decrease in cash and cash equivalents

The closing balance of cash and cash equivalents, calculated as the opening balance plus net increase/decrease in cash and cash equivalents.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Cash and Cash Equivalents at the End of the Period
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cash and Cash Equivalents at the End of the Period in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow Statement Preparation
text:
Cash Flow Statement Preparation

Key terms: Cash Flow Statement, Dividends, Financing Activities

A cash flow statement is prepared from the statement of profit and loss. Dividends paid are adjusted in financing activities only.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cash Flow Statement Preparation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash and Cash Equivalents
text:
Cash and Cash Equivalents

Key terms: Cash, Cash Equivalents, Cash Flow Statement

Cash and cash equivalents consist of cash in hand, balances with banks, and investments in money-market instruments. They are reported on the cash flow statement.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash and Cash Equivalents in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Receipts from Customers
text:
Cash Receipts from Customers

Key terms: Cash Receipts, Sales, Trade Receivables

Cash receipts from customers are calculated by adding trade receivables at the beginning of the year to sales, then subtracting trade receivables at the end of the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cash Receipts from Customers in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Paid to Suppliers and Employees
text:
Cash Paid to Suppliers and Employees

Key terms: Cash Paid, Suppliers, Employees, Trade Payables, Inventories

Cash paid to suppliers and employees is calculated by adding cost of revenue from operations, administrative and selling expenses, trade payables at the beginning of the year, and inventories at the end of the year. Then, subtract trade payables at the end of the year and inventories at the beginning of the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Cash Paid to Suppliers and Employees
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Cash Paid to Suppliers and Employees in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Income Tax Paid
text:
Income Tax Paid

Key terms: Income Tax, Income Tax Expense, Income Tax Liability, Income Tax Payable

Income tax paid includes the income tax expense for the year, plus the income tax liability at the beginning of the year, minus the income tax payable at the end of the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Income Tax Paid in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Repayment of Long-term Borrowings
text:
Repayment of Long-term Borrowings

Key terms: Long-term Borrowings, Repayment, Long-term Debts

Repayment of long-term borrowings is calculated by adding long-term borrowings made during the year to the long-term debts at the beginning of the year, then subtracting the long-term borrowings at the end of the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Repayment of Long-term Borrowings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest Paid
text:
Interest Paid

Key terms: Interest, Interest Expense, Interest Payable

Interest paid is calculated by adding the interest expense for the year to the interest payable at the beginning of the year, then subtracting the interest payable at the end of the year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest Paid in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital
text:
Share Capital

Key terms: Shareholders, Shares, Funds

Share capital is the money invested in a company by its shareholders in exchange for shares. It's a key source of a company's funds.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Share Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Reserve and Surplus
text:
Reserve and Surplus

Key terms: Reserve, Surplus, Profit

Reserve and surplus are amounts set aside from a company's profits for future use. They are not distributed as dividends to shareholders.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Reserve and Surplus in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Current Liabilities
text:
Current Liabilities

Key terms: Trade Payables, Short-term Provisions, Debts

Current liabilities are debts that a company is expected to pay off within one year. They include trade payables and short-term provisions.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Current Liabilities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Cash Flow Statement
text:
Cash Flow Statement

Key terms: Cash Inflows, Cash Outflows, Operating Activities, Investing Activities, Financing Activities

A cash flow statement is a financial statement that shows the inflows and outflows of cash through a company's operating, investing, and financing activities.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cash Flow Statement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Depreciation
text:
Depreciation

Key terms: Tangible Asset, Useful Life, Balance Sheet

Depreciation is an accounting method of allocating the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life. It's not a cash outflow but reduces the value of the asset on the balance sheet.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Depreciation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Dividend
text:
Dividend

Key terms: Shareholders, Profits, Cash Payment

A dividend is a distribution of a company's profits to its shareholders. It's usually a cash payment, but can also be in the form of additional shares.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Dividend in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Balance Sheet
text:
Balance Sheet

Key terms: Assets, Liabilities, Equity

A balance sheet is a financial statement that provides a snapshot of a company's assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Balance Sheet in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Operating Activities
text:
Operating Activities

Key terms: Revenue, Production, Sales

Operating activities are the core revenue-producing activities of a company's business. They include activities like production, sales, and servicing of products.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Operating Activities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Company Types
text:
Company Types

Key terms: public company, private company, government-owned company

Companies can be public, private, or government-owned. Public companies have shares listed on a stock exchange, private companies do not, and government-owned companies are owned by the state.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Company Types in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Capital
text:
Share Capital

Key terms: share capital, shareholders

Share capital is the money contributed by shareholders in exchange for shares in a company. It's the company's basic financial resource.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Share Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Classes
text:
Share Classes

Key terms: equity shares, preference shares

Shares can be equity or preference. Equity shares have voting rights and preference shares have priority in receiving dividends but no voting rights.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Share Classes in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Share Issue
text:
Share Issue

Key terms: rights issue, public issue, bonus issue

A company can issue new shares to raise capital. This can be done through a rights issue, a public issue, or a bonus issue.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Share Issue in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Debentures
text:
Debentures

Key terms: debentures, secured, unsecured

Debentures are long-term loans taken by a company, with interest paid regularly. They can be secured or unsecured.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Debentures in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Financial Statements
text:
Financial Statements

Key terms: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement

Financial statements include the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement. They provide information about a company's financial health.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Financial Statements in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Financial Statement Analysis
text:
Financial Statement Analysis

Key terms: comparative statements, common size statements

Analyzing financial statements helps understand a company's performance, liquidity, solvency, and profitability. Tools include comparative statements and common size statements.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Financial Statement Analysis in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Accounting Ratios
text:
Accounting Ratios

Key terms: liquidity ratios, solvency ratios, activity ratios, profitability ratios

Accounting ratios help evaluate a company's performance. They include liquidity ratios, solvency ratios, activity ratios, and profitability ratios.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Accounting Ratios in Grade 12 Accountancy.
